newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Energy Africa interim shr down, sales up.
newsitem.headline: Energy Africa interim shr down, sales up.

text.p: Full name: Energy Africa (oil exploration company)
NOTE - The company said the exceptional item last year was due to the cancellation of debt by parent company Engen Ltd and sale of licences.
The group said cashflow had risen 136 percent to 98.2 million rand, while net production averaged 10,200 barrels per day, an increase of 53 percent.

Production was expected to increase by about 3,000 barrels per day once the Oribi oilfield off South Africa came on stream, probably in May. Energy Africa owns 20 percent of the joint venture with the rest held by state-owned Soekor.
Further exploration activities were being explored but the group said that the first half results would not necessarily be repeated in the second half because of the weaker oil price.
The company said it expected to continue re-investing surplus funds for some years rather than declare a dividend.
